name: Gate-switched superconducting logic
subtitle: computer switches that turn superconductivity on and off

effects.effect: two graphene sheets twisted by 1.1 degrees become a superconductor
very cold metals lose all electrical resistance

effect: two graphene sheets twisted by 1.1 degrees become a superconductor
how: Computing burns ever more electricity, and every ordinary transistor wastes some as heat each time it switches. In two graphene sheets twisted by just over one degree, a small voltage on a nearby plate turns superconductivity on and off, so each switch either carries current with zero loss or blocks it, making logic that wastes almost nothing.
obstacle: It works only within about two degrees of absolute zero, and twisting sheets to exactly the right angle cannot yet be done by the million.
why: Gate-switched twisted-graphene superconductivity shown in single devices; no circuit built from them.
real: Gate-defined Josephson junctions and tunnelling transistors in magic-angle graphene were built (Rodan-Legrain 2021), but no superconducting logic circuit.
